## Overview

The `hashicorp/boundary` GitHub repository, which holds Boundary Community Edition (CE), has been archived. The project's [README](https://github.com/hashicorp/boundary/blob/main/README.md) states: "Boundary Community Edition (CE) is no longer under active development, and this repository has been archived as of October 8, 2026." editor_notes.source_verification: Fetched the PR ref refs/pull/2620/head (no branch checkout needed) and extracted the single submission file by title; the PR contains exactly one file, 2026-10-13T13-58-11Z_hashicorp-archives-the-boundary-community-edition-.json, whose title matches the PR title; no stray files. chief:review: hash valid, signature valid, all checks pass, no suspicious_patterns on any source. Read all four gzipped snapshots (text-extracted): all four exist, status 200, and contain page body, not chrome only. source-0.html.gz (repo page): archived banner 'This repository was archived by the owner on Oct 9, 2026. It is now read-only.', README rendered in full, 'Public archive' label; confirms the overview paragraph. source-1.html.gz (README.md): verbatim 'Boundary Community Edition (CE) is no longer under active development, and this repository has been archived as of October 8, 2026.'; 'Future Boundary development will focus on HCP Boundary and Boundary Enterprise, where we can provide enterprise grade human and agentic access capabilities.'; 'This repository is now read-only and no longer accepts new issues, pull requests, or community contributions.'; 'No new Boundary CE releases, maintenance updates, bug fixes, or security patches are currently planned.'; 'Teams continuing to use Boundary CE should evaluate whether it meets their operational, security, and compliance requirements.' All article quotes and paraphrases match; the paraphrase of existing code and binaries remaining available 'for reference and existing self-managed use' is accurate. The README names no author (confirmed). source-2.html.gz (LICENSE): Licensor International Business Machines Corporation (IBM); Licensed Work 'Boundary Version 0.14.0 or later'; Additional Use Grant text including 'in order to compete with IBM Corp's paid version(s) of the Licensed Work' verified verbatim; Change Date 'Four years from the date the Licensed Work is published'; Change License MPL 2.0; Business Source License 1.1. source-3.html.gz (CHANGELOG.md, 2562 lines): top entry '0.21.3 (2026/04/28)' with Security entry 'Resolved a vulnerability (CVE-2026-7776) that could lead to a denial-of-service condition during TLS handshakes.' matches the quoted fragment. Live verification (curl and GitHub API, 2026-10-13): raw README identical to the snapshot text; live repo page still shows the Oct 9 archived banner and the same README; API archived=true, pushed_at 2026-10-09T16:50:40Z, updated_at 2026-10-13T00:09:15Z, license NOASSERTION; the README was last changed by commit eeb38a1a 'Revise README for Boundary CE archiving (#6788)' on 2026-10-09T16:50:36Z by GitHub user learhy (profile: Dan Rohan, company @hashicorp; not a verified org-membership lookup, the org member API returned 404 to our unauthenticated-for-org query), which supports treating the README as HashiCorp's own text and hence 'Saying' in the title. No un-archive or further statement observed. The date discrepancy is real: README text says Oct 8, the README commit and archive flag are Oct 9 UTC; the article reports both without resolving them, which is the honest treatment.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Title: 'Archives ... Repository' backed by GitHub's archived banner and API flag; 'Saying No New Releases or Security Patches Are Currently Planned' tracks the README wording exactly (the 'currently planned' hedge is preserved). Releases API shows v0.21.3 (published 2026-04-30, marked latest; v0.20.3 and v0.19.5 same day), consistent with the changelog top entry (dated 04/28); the article states only what the CHANGELOG says, so no error; adding the release date was optional. The sentence that fixes for later CE vulnerabilities are 'not something the README leads users to expect' is a restrained inference, flagged by 'Because the README says'. No legal conclusion about forks is drawn; the article expressly declines to. Vendor claims are attributed to the README. The HashiCorp forum post and the Hacker News thread are not used or referenced anywhere in the article.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributive, no AI self-reference, no editorializing. 'agentic' appears only inside a direct quote.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Boundary coverage in the archive (grep of src/content/articles). Related prior coverage: the File Browser archival (2026-08/02) and the HCP Terraform free-tier end under IBM (2026-03/03), linked in article-meta related_articles as context. Not a duplicate.
concerns: Summary says 'no new CE releases or security patches planned' and drops the README's 'currently'; the title and body keep the hedge. Minor, judged not to need a correction since the headline and body carry the exact wording.
Allowlist: all four sources are github.com, already on config/source_allowlist.txt; no change made.
recommendations: Summaries should keep hedges such as 'currently' when the headline does.
Optionally note the v0.21.3 release date (2026-04-30, per the releases page) when reporting the last release.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-hedged briefing resting entirely on the vendor's own repository files and saying so. All claims trace to snapshots read in full and re-checked live. APPROVE.
